Wausau Winter Farmers Market returns with new SNAP benefit matching program
The indoor market runs Saturdays through April at John Marshall Elementary School, offering locally grown food and a new program that doubles eligible shoppers’ purchasing power. 
 by Shereen Siewert November 4, 2026 November 4, 2026 Share this:

 Upscaled with Gigapixel v1.3.1. 3390x1900 => 5536x3103 (1.63304x) Model: High Fidelity V2, denoise: 0.07154390504560637, sharpen: 0.01, decompression: 0.01 WAUSAU — The Wausau Winter Farmers Market is returning for another season, with a new program that will help shoppers receiving FoodShare benefits stretch their grocery budgets. The indoor market will operate from 9 a.m. to noon Saturdays, November through April, in the gym at John Marshall Elementary School, 1918 Lamont St. Parking and entrances are available along Weston and Broadway avenues. Shoppers can find a variety of locally produced foods throughout the winter, including carrots, onions, potatoes, cabbage, garlic, mushrooms, greens, eggs, beef, pork, chicken, honey, maple syrup, cheese, bread and other baked goods. New this season is a dollar-for-dollar matching program for customers using Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program benefits, known in Wisconsin as FoodShare. The program provides up to $20 in matching funds for the purchase of fruits and vegetables.
 “The matching program helps customers stretch their grocery budget. At the Wausau Winter Market, you are welcomed, no matter how you pay for food,” said Meliss Haack, regional farmers market coordinator. FoodShare customers can visit the market’s information booth to swipe their electronic benefit transfer cards and receive tokens accepted by vendors. Tokens do not expire and may be used at subsequent winter markets, although organizers encourage customers to spend them before the season ends in April. Customers who prefer to pay by credit or debit card can also purchase tokens at the information booth for a $2 transaction fee.
 Organizers note that the winter market operates a separate token system from the Wausau Summer Farmers Market. Tokens purchased at the summer market cannot be used at the winter location. The matching program also supports local agricultural producers by encouraging shoppers to purchase food directly from area farms. “This program benefits our farmers and community,” said Holden Flaig, a market board member and owner of Farm Time Out, which sells grass-fed beef and lettuce. “Having customers spend their SNAP dollars with small farms keeps money in our local economy and healthy food goes to our community, a win-win for everyone!”
 All vendors at the winter market accept the market’s tokens as payment. Help Us Keep Local Journalism Alive
